definitions.explanation: The number ten. A base number in Japanese counting, used to form larger numbers (11 = じゅういち, 20 = にじゅう, etc.). Very consistent in pronunciation across most combinations.

examples.japanese: {十|じゅう}{分|ぷん}で{着|つ}きます。
{十|じゅう}{人|にん}のクラスです。
examples.english: It's a class of ten people.

examples.japanese: {十|じゅう}{月|がつ}は{秋|あき}なので{涼|すず}しいです。
examples.english: October is autumn, so it's cool.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{十|じゅう}{時間|じかん}{以上|いじょう}{仕事|しごと}をしたので、とても{疲|つか}れました。
examples.english: I worked more than ten hours today, so I'm very tired.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{十|じゅう}{時|じ}から{十二|じゅうに}{時|じ}まで{日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}をして、{午後|ごご}は{図書館|としょかん}で{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいます。
examples.english: Every morning I study Japanese from ten to twelve o'clock, and in the afternoon I hang out with friends.

notes: The native counter is {十|とお} (too). じゅう is used to build larger numbers: {二|に}{十|じゅう} (nijuu, 20), {三|さん}{十|じゅう} (sanjuu, 30), etc. When combined with certain counters, じゅう may become じゅっ or じっ: {十|じゅっ}{本|ぽん} (juppon), {十|じっ}{歳|さい} (jissai, 10 years old).
